name: journal-the-three-wishes.json
content:
Three men were granted one wish each by a judge: Jesus, Paul and a Muslim.

Jesus went first. Jesus said, “I wish to go home.”

The judge granted his wish and sent him home.

Paul went next. Paul said, “I wish to go home too!”

The judge granted his wish, and Paul went home as well.

Finally, it was the Muslim’s turn.

The judge asked, “And what is your wish?”

The Muslim smiled and said:

“Your Honour, I wish for both of them to come back!”

The judge looked confused. “Why would you do that?”

The Muslim replied:

“Because Jesus is supposed to come back for his Second Coming, and Paul still has some explaining to do!”

Moral of the joke: never give a Muslim the last wish!

Why the joke works

The punchline rests on two things in the record. Paul told the Thessalonians that he expected to be alive when Christ returned (1 Thessalonians 4:15-17), and the return did not come in his lifetime. See [paulus_link slug="paul-and-the-return-that-failed" /].

The explaining that Paul owes is the case this site sets out, count by count. See [paulus_link slug="the-measure" /].
